A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original Gaussian-to-Swiss-Roll and weather experiments in Section 5, plus neural-parameterization and colored-MNIST experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds FSBM comparisons and additional weather results.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly outlines a finite-category adaptation using a vector-valued potential, neural cost and finite-sum partition function. This is an unevaluated extension; the continuous-data loss, Gaussian parameterization, training procedure and Appendix A algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Evaluation retains Gaussian-to-Swiss-Roll translation, weather prediction and colored MNIST. Additional weather cases vary sample counts. Discrete targets and the applications discussed in Appendix B are not accompanied by evaluations.

E2.justification: FSBM, already cited in v3, becomes an evaluated comparator in both Swiss-Roll experiments, appearing in Figures 2 and 5 and Table 3. Existing comparators remain, including GNOT despite its panel relocation. Weather comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Weather Table 1 extends the experimental grid with five paired samples and five unpaired samples. Previously reported settings, data preparation, test split, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged; FSBM joins the existing small-data and 16K Swiss-Roll settings.

E4.justification: The weather data-quantity analysis now probes more extreme scarcity. The existing 16K sanity check also evaluates whether additional data resolves FSBM's conditional-mapping failure. Figure 6's source-versus-target-data ablation and the neural-parameterization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report plus/minus values without specifying run counts, seeds or how these uncertainties were estimated. Additional weather entries follow the existing practice; no new statistical estimation or testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V4 adds weather entries and FSBM findings, while retaining all shared weather scores and Table 2. The new five-pair row reports LL 17.91±0.07 with 250 unpaired samples and 9.40±0.03 with 500. Figure 2 also swaps the existing images assigned to CondNF and CondNF (SS), without explaining the reassignment.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds formal weak-OT definitions, alternative dual formulations and a derivation connecting EOT with the static Schrödinger bridge problem. The central propositions, universal-approximation assumptions and proofs are unchanged, with v3 Appendix D becoming v4 Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: a joint paired/unpaired likelihood objective, its inverse-EOT equivalence, tractable Gaussian parameterization and universal approximation. The discrete extension is presented as a future direction.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands explanations of choosing entropic OT, discrete-target applicability, structured-output difficulties and practical applications. It adds extreme-low-data overfitting limitations and hypothesizes that key-point costs bias OTCS and FSBM. Section 5.2 shifts emphasis from increasing data improving performance to gains from small amounts of unpaired data.

D1.justification: V4 newly reports 2,668 learnable parameters for the weather model, explains that architecture was held fixed across Table 1, and supplies an FSBM implementation link. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training times and code-availability statements are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially broadens positioning through detailed relationships to previous inverse-EOT likelihood formulations, including Andrade et al. (2025), and additional discrete-model and application literature. The existing OT-solver review moves from Section 4 to Appendix B.4.

P1.justification: V4 adds appendix navigation and expanded explanations, relocates OT-related work, and selectively rewrites the background, weather discussion and broader-impact paragraph. Affiliations, citation style and an LLM-use disclosure also change. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: A different document template changes the title and author layout, heading typography and running headers throughout. Figures 2 and 5 expand to fifteen-panel grids with reordered comparators; Tables 1 and 3 expand, Table 2 becomes a standalone centered display, and an appendix contents list is added.

improvement.justification: The added FSBM comparisons, extreme-low-data results and fuller OT and applicability explanations modestly strengthen the paper's evidence and context. Reporting ambiguities limit the gain: Figure 2's CondNF panel reassignment is unexplained, and Appendix C.3 attributes divergence to 'our method' although the corresponding Table 1 cell is labeled 'Baseline'. The central proofs and established quantitative results remain unchanged.
